channel.title: N722BD Accident Monitor (EN)
channel.description: Running overview of public information on the Learjet 60 N722BD accident in Palm Beach County, Florida (1 Nov 2026). Distinguishes official, data, media and unconfirmed reports.

item.title: [Unconfirmed] NTSB reportedly recovers cockpit voice recorder; excavation complete
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (article not read directly), NTSB said on 9 Nov it found the cockpit voice recorder at the initial impact site and sent it to its Washington lab; crater excavation is complete. The recording's content and release timing are unknown. The NTSB preliminary report has not been published yet. (Source: WPTV)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] NTSB: crater excavation continues, part of an engine found
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (article not read directly), NTSB said on 5 Nov that excavation of the impact site continues and a portion of one engine was recovered; wreckage will go to a secure location. Whether the cockpit voice recorder was found is not stated in the available results. The NTSB preliminary report is expected within ~30 days of the crash and has not been published yet. (Source: CBS12 (WPEC))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Per search results: NTSB named operator Aurora Aviation (Upper Jet), investigation ERA27MA026
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (page not read directly), the NTSB reportedly named Aurora Aviation, doing business as Upper Jet, as the operator, with the investigation numbered ERA27MA026. This differs from the earlier mention of East Coast Jets (u012), and the flight regime remains unconfirmed. No NTSB information newer than the 2 Nov briefing was found. (Source: WFTV (Orlando))

item.title: [Media] Fox News: jet had a cockpit voice recorder but NTSB has not found it yet; ex-investigator considers structural overstress
item.description: [Media] According to Fox News (read directly), the aircraft had a cockpit voice recorder, but investigators have not found it and cannot confirm it was aboard at the time of the crash. The crew reported icing and moderate turbulence at about 35,000 ft shortly before the rapid loss of altitude. Former NTSB investigator Greg Feith, in his own opinion and not an NTSB finding, said a pilot may have tried to level the jet and overstressed the structure. This is a media report; the NTSB's own text was not read directly. (Source: Fox News)

item.title: [Media] ABC: NTSB found left elevator 1.3–3.8 miles from the impact site
item.description: [Media] According to ABC News (read directly), NTSB member Tom Chapman said at Tuesday's briefing that most of the left elevator was found in three pieces 1.3 to 3.8 miles from the crash site, so parts separated before impact. It is unclear whether losing the elevator contributed to the crash or whether forces in the descent above certified maximum speed caused the separation. Investigators were to enter the crater in the roadway on Wednesday. This is a media report citing the NTSB; the NTSB's own text was not read directly. (Source: ABC News)

item.title: [Media] AP/PBS: aircraft began breaking up in the air, NTSB says
item.description: [Media] According to an AP report (read directly on PBS NewsHour), NTSB member Tom Chapman said evidence suggests the aircraft started to break up before impact and that wreckage may lie farther from the impact site; the extent and timing of any separation are not yet determined. Experts quoted by AP mention possible detachment of tail parts in turbulence or the dive – this is speculation. Investigators will focus heavily on weather. (Source: PBS NewsHour (AP))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Operator: East Coast Jets reportedly confirmed a crew member's death (per search results)
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (article not read directly), East Coast Jets confirmed that a crew member is among the victims; WPTV and CBS12 carry tributes from loved ones. This does not confirm the flight regime (Part 91 / 135) and the company's relationship to the flight must be verified. Crew names are not published. (Source: WPTV)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] NTSB briefing: crew reported ice and turbulence, then overspeed and rapid descent
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (a CBS12 article on the ice and turbulence report; content not read directly, not confirmed by other sources), an NTSB board member said at Monday's briefing that the crew reported light clear ice and moderate turbulence shortly before the crash, followed by an overspeed and a steep descent. A crater filled with water hampers access to the wreckage; about 20 investigators are on scene and the cause is undetermined. Local officials say the road may stay closed a month or more. (Source: CBS12 (WPEC))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] WPTV: 77 mobile homes remain displaced, Military Trail may be closed for weeks
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (page not read directly), about 77 mobile homes remain displaced after Monday's news conference by officials and NTSB members, and residents do not know when they can return. Military Trail between Cresthaven Blvd and 10th Avenue North may stay closed for weeks; the cause of the crash has not been determined. (Source: WPTV)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] CBS12: about 600 residents remain displaced; NTSB to hold briefing
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (page not read directly), around 600 Greenacres residents remain displaced or assisted by authorities after the crash, and the NTSB is due to hold a briefing in West Palm Beach on Monday. Results also mention a Bombardier statement supporting the investigation; the cause and any role of weather are not yet determined. (Source: CBS12 (WPEC))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Operator and flight rules (Part 91 / 135) unclear
item.description: [Unconfirmed] IBTimes UK reports that N722BD appears in charter listings under Aurora Aviation's Part 135 certificate, but officials have not confirmed whether the flight was a charter; Austin airport described the aircraft as private. Unconfirmed, single source. Discrepancy: serial number 60-271 (registry / IBTimes) vs 60-186 (charter site FlyUSA, per search results). (Source: International Business Times UK)

item.title: [Data] Registered owner of N722BD: LR60271 LLC (Wilmington, DE)
item.description: [Data] FlightAware (read directly) lists LR60271 LLC of Wilmington, Delaware, as owner of N722BD; flight history is hidden at the owner/operator's request. The registered owner does not show who operated the flight. (Source: FlightAware)

item.title: [Media] FlightGlobal: “high-energy” accident, photo of responders at scene
item.description:
[Media] FlightGlobal (only the intro read directly, rest behind paywall) calls it a high-energy accident after a high-speed dive; US investigators are starting a probe. The article carries a photo of emergency services at the scene. (Source: FlightGlobal)
Photo: Emergency services at the accident site (Palm Beach County Fire Rescue, via FlightGlobal)

item.title: [Media] ABC: impact near Military Trail in Greenacres, descent about 350 ft/s
item.description:
[Media] Citing the FAA, ABC News reports a rapid descent of about 350 feet per second; the aircraft was 22 years old. According to local authorities it came down near Military Trail between Cresthaven Blvd and 10th Avenue in the Greenacres area, leaving a crater near a shopping centre. (Source: ABC News)
Photo: Flames at the crash site, Palm Beach County, 1 Nov 2026 (Eduin Cruz / Reuters, via ABC News)

item.title: [Media] NBC: all 9 on board killed; ATC audio with mayday call
item.description: [Media] According to NBC News, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said all 9 people on board died; the victims have not been identified. NBC describes ATC audio in which the crew reports light ice and moderate turbulence, then a mayday and descent of 10,000 and later 20,000 ft/min. Governor DeSantis said, per NBC, there were no reports of injuries on the ground. (Source: NBC News)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] NTSB launching go-team, briefing Monday in West Palm Beach
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (the X post was not read directly), the NTSB announced a go-team; investigators were due on Sunday and Monday morning, with a media briefing on Monday in West Palm Beach. Location wording differs between sources: NTSB “Lake Worth Beach”, FAA “Cresthaven”, sheriff Military Trail between Cresthaven Blvd and 10th Ave N. (Source: NTSB Newsroom (X))

item.title: [Data] FR24: steep right-hand descent, last return 8,750 ft at 17:49:22Z
item.description: [Data] According to FR24 ADS-B data (read directly), N722BD (Learjet 60, built 2004) departed Austin at 15:37Z; at 17:48Z it briefly climbed, then entered a steep right-hand descent. The last altitude received was 8,750 ft at 17:49:22Z, with vertical rate above 32,000 ft/min. In ATC audio reviewed by FR24, the crew had earlier reported icing, moderate turbulence and precipitation and requested a climb to FL370. (Source: Flightradar24 Blog)

item.title: [Official] FAA: Learjet 60 crashed near Cresthaven, 9 people on board
item.description: [Official] According to the FAA statement (read directly), a Learjet 60 crashed into a residential area near Cresthaven, Florida, at about 12:50 local time on 1 Nov. It was flying from Austin-Bergstrom (Texas) to North Eleuthera (Bahamas) with 9 people on board. The NTSB leads the investigation with FAA involvement. (Source: FAA – Newsroom)
